title: What is RAG
text: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) combines a retriever that fetches relevant documents from a knowledge base with a large language model that generates an answer grounded in those documents.

title: Chunking
text: Chunking splits long documents into smaller passages before embedding. Chunk size and chunk overlap strongly affect retrieval quality in a RAG pipeline.

title: Embeddings
text: Embeddings are dense vectors that represent the meaning of text. Similar texts have embeddings that are close together under cosine similarity.

title: Vector databases
text: Vector databases such as ChromaDB, Pinecone, Qdrant and pgvector store embeddings and support fast approximate nearest neighbour search.

title: BM25
text: BM25 is a sparse keyword retrieval algorithm that scores documents using term frequency, inverse document frequency and document length normalisation.

title: Hybrid search
text: Hybrid search combines dense vector retrieval with sparse keyword retrieval like BM25, often merging results with reciprocal rank fusion.

title: Reranking
text: A reranker such as a cross-encoder re-scores the top retrieved documents so the most relevant passages move to the first positions before generation.

title: Hallucination
text: Hallucination happens when a language model generates content that is not supported by the retrieved context or by facts. Faithfulness metrics detect hallucination.

title: Why evaluate retrieval
text: If the retriever does not fetch the right documents, the generator cannot produce a correct grounded answer. Retrieval evaluation is therefore the first step of RAG evaluation.

title: Precision and recall
text: Precision at k measures how many of the top k retrieved documents are relevant. Recall at k measures how many of all relevant documents appear in the top k.

title: MRR
text: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) averages one divided by the rank of the first relevant document across queries. It rewards putting a relevant document at the very top.

title: NDCG
text: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) uses graded relevance and discounts gains logarithmically by rank, comparing the ranking to an ideal ordering.

title: LangGraph
text: LangGraph is a framework for building stateful multi-agent workflows as graphs, often used to orchestrate retrieval, grading and generation steps in agentic RAG.

title: Golden dataset
text: A golden evaluation dataset contains questions, the ids of the relevant documents and reference answers. It is the ground truth used to score a RAG system.

title: FastAPI
text: FastAPI is a Python web framework for building APIs quickly with type hints, commonly used to serve RAG pipelines as REST endpoints.
